protocols.clinicalDefinitionEn: Generalized weakness/fatigue assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance. Adult patient. Male.
protocols.backgroundInfoEn: Persistent unexplained fatigue can be associated with sleep problems, mood disorders, anaemia, diabetes, thyroid disease, infection, or other medical conditions. Sudden focal weakness, chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, confusion, or reduced responsiveness is an emergency presentation. Fatigue lasting weeks or interfering with normal life warrants clinical assessment.

initialAssessmentQuestions.promptTextEn: What is the person's exact age and sex, are they pregnant/recently postpartum, and did weakness start suddenly or gradually? Clarify generalized versus one-sided/focal weakness and child feeding, behaviour, urine, and safeguarding concerns.
Any unintentional weight loss, mood changes, or other new symptoms?
Is this affecting daily activities?

questions.questionTextEn: Is there sudden one-sided weakness or numbness, slurred speech, chest pain, severe difficulty breathing, or is the person confused or difficult to rouse?
questions.rationaleEn: Universal emergency rule-out added ahead of the tiredness/fatigue guidance itself - sudden focal weakness or altered consciousness may indicate stroke or another acute emergency rather than simple fatigue.

questions.questionTextEn: Has the tiredness lasted a few weeks without a clear cause, is it affecting daily life, or is it accompanied by weight loss, mood changes, or gasping/snorting/choking sounds during sleep?
questions.rationaleEn: NHS.UK guidance recommends a primary-care review for unexplained, persistent, or functionally-impairing tiredness, or tiredness with these associated symptoms.

questions.questionTextEn: Is this a normal, occasional tiredness with a clear cause and none of the features above?
questions.rationaleEn: NHS.UK guidance: it's normal to feel tired sometimes; sleep hygiene and lifestyle measures are appropriate first steps.

careAdvice.instructionTextEn: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for sudden or one-sided weakness, inability to stand, confusion, fainting, seizure, abnormal breathing, chest pain, major bleeding, severe infection, pregnancy/postpartum danger signs, suspected poisoning, or an unwell/floppy child. Keep the person still and do not give food, drink, or medicine if consciousness or swallowing is impaired. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care. Call Back If: worsening or one-sided weakness; loss of consciousness, seizure, or confusion; abnormal breathing, chest pain, bleeding, or severe infection.
Book a routine primary-care review to investigate persistent or unexplained tiredness. Call Back If: new symptoms develop; worsening weight loss.

Maintain a balanced diet and regular activity, keep consistent sleep times aiming for 6-9 hours, relax before bed, and avoid smoking, excess alcohol, caffeine, and screens close to bedtime. Call Back If: tiredness persists for weeks; new symptoms develop.

guidelineRedirects.promptTextEn: Is a measured blood-glucose reading below 4 mmol/L, or are symptoms suggesting hypoglycaemia, in a person with diabetes?
guidelineRedirects.hintEn: Resolved from alias: Diabetes - Low Blood Sugar

guidelineRedirects.promptTextEn: Is a measured blood-glucose reading high, with thirst, frequent urination, vomiting, abdominal pain, drowsiness, or other hyperglycaemia symptoms?
guidelineRedirects.hintEn: Resolved from alias: Diabetes - High Blood Sugar

keyPointsEn: Persistent unexplained fatigue can be associated with sleep problems, mood disorders, anaemia, diabetes, thyroid disease, infection, or other medical conditions.
Sudden focal weakness, chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, confusion, or reduced responsiveness is an emergency presentation.
Fatigue lasting weeks or interfering with normal life warrants clinical assessment.

Keep the person still and do not give food, drink, or medicine if consciousness or swallowing is impaired. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

protocols.clinicalDefinitionEn: Unintentional weight loss assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance. Adult patient. Female.

initialAssessmentQuestions.promptTextEn: What is the person's exact age and sex, are they pregnant/recently postpartum, and what dated measured weights, units, time course, and growth trend are available? This protocol starts at age 12; younger children require an approved pediatric route.

Was weight loss truly unintended? Ask privately and age-appropriately about food restriction, purging, laxatives/diuretics, excessive exercise, body-image distress, food insecurity, neglect/coercion, pregnancy, medicines/substances, and self-harm/safeguarding risk.

Ask about inability to eat/drink, repeated vomiting/diarrhoea, dehydration/reduced urine, fainting, confusion, chest symptoms, severe weakness, fever/night sweats, pain, bleeding, swallowing difficulty, persistent cough, excessive thirst/urination, abdominal symptoms, and other new illness.

questions.questionTextEn: Is there inability to keep fluids down, severe dehydration or very little urine, fainting/collapse, confusion, seizure, chest pain, abnormal breathing, severe weakness/inability to stand, major bleeding, severe abdominal pain, suspected diabetic crisis, dangerous eating-disorder behaviour, or immediate self-harm/safeguarding danger?
questions.rationaleEn: Unintended weight loss is usually gradual, but acute dehydration, metabolic illness, bleeding, severe malnutrition/electrolyte disturbance, medical instability, or mental-health/safeguarding danger can be time-critical.

questions.questionTextEn: With emergency features excluded, is measured weight continuing to fall without intent, is there another symptom or medicine change, or is the person aged 12-17, pregnant/postpartum, medically vulnerable, possibly restricting/purging, or affected by food insecurity or safeguarding concerns?
questions.rationaleEn: NHS.UK guidance: arrange a primary-care review as soon as possible if there is weight loss and other symptoms - the earlier the cause is found, the sooner it can be treated; weight loss without trying should always be checked.

careAdvice.titleEn: Qatar emergency response for acute instability
careAdvice.instructionTextEn: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive. Keep the person supervised and at rest. Do not force food or fluids, give supplements/electrolytes, or alter insulin/other medicines when vomiting, confused, drowsy, unsafe to swallow, or medically unstable. For immediate self-harm or safeguarding danger, follow the approved emergency safety and welfare-check pathway. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care. Call Back If: collapse, confusion, seizure, or inability to stand; abnormal breathing, chest pain, severe dehydration, bleeding, or severe abdominal pain; unsafe eating-disorder behaviour or self-harm risk.

Arrange prompt in-person assessment through the Qatar route and timing approved by governance. Bring dated weights/growth records and a complete medicine/supplement history. Do not prescribe high-calorie supplements, electrolytes, vitamins, appetite stimulants, laxative changes, or refeeding targets without assessment; rapid refeeding can be unsafe in severe malnutrition. Adolescents require private age-appropriate eating-disorder and safeguarding screening with approved caregiver involvement. Call Back If: weight loss accelerates; fainting, vomiting, dehydration, weakness, chest symptoms, bleeding, fever/night sweats, excessive thirst/urination, or self-harm concern.

guidelineRedirects.promptTextEn: Is intentional food restriction, fear of weight gain, purging, or a suspected eating disorder the main concern?
guidelineRedirects.hintEn: Resolved from alias: Eating Disorder Concerns

firstAid.instructionTextEn: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive. Keep the person supervised and at rest. Do not force food or fluids, give supplements/electrolytes, or alter insulin/other medicines when vomiting, confused, drowsy, unsafe to swallow, or medically unstable. For immediate self-harm or safeguarding danger, follow the approved emergency safety and welfare-check pathway. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
